title: Majestic Opposition
summary: Retreat to the right square so the pawn race avoids a skewer and a pawn sacrifice gains opposition.

nodes.question: Which retreat keeps the draw?
nodes.explanation: White has Kb3 and b2 against Kd3 and f7. The black king shoulders White away from the pawn; the saving move is Ka2 in the saved board, not captioned Ka1.

exercises.prompt: Why does the apparently passive retreat help?
exercises.answer: Ka2 makes room for the b-pawn and avoids the queen skewer that occurs with the king on a3. It also permits Kb3 opposition after the pawn sacrifice.

exercises.prompt: Why sacrifice b5 instead of protecting it?
exercises.answer: After ...Kxb5 Kb3, White gains opposition and can reach the f-pawn’s promotion path in time to draw.

startContext: The complete four-piece source root is visually reconstructed. Saved boards correct captioned Ka1 to Ka2 and show ...Kc4 before the pawn sacrifice. The opposition and losing Ka3 skewer lines are source-based; the direct drawn promotion race is an independently supplied representative connection. Every encoded position is checked exactly.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: The automatic captions name Ka1 as the saving retreat.
sourceCorrections.correction: The initial saved board has White Kb3. Stable later images show Ka2; Ka1 is not a legal single king move from b3.
